subject: general
question: In File Explorer of Windows 10, the keyboard shortcut 'Num Lock + Asterisk sign (*)' is used to ___________.

options.text: display all subfolders under the selected folder
open the properties dialog box for the selected item
display the contents of the selected folder

solution:
The correct answer is __**display all subfolders under the selected folder**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Expand all subfolders under the selected folder**

 
 
• Num Lock + Asterisk sign (*) in File Explorer is used to expand all subfolders under the selected folder.
 
• This shortcut allows users to view the entire directory structure within a folder quickly.
 
• It is especially useful for navigating complex directory trees with many nested subfolders.
 
• By expanding all subfolders at once, users can efficiently locate specific files or folders without manually opening each subfolder.
 
• This shortcut saves time and effort, enhancing the user experience when managing files.
 
• It is an effective way to get an overview of the folder structure and contents.
